extraction.name: FLORES-101
extraction.description: The FLORES-101 evaluation benchmark for low-resource and multilingual machine translation, consisting of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and covering a variety of different topics and domains, translated in 101 languages by professional translators.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc'Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzman, Angela Fan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Sentences were sourced from English Wikipedia (Wikinews, Wikijunior, WikiVoyage). The selection process involved selecting an article at random and manually selecting 3-5 contiguous sentences. The data was then translated by professional translators through Language Service Providers (LSPs) with a controlled workflow including automatic checks and human evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Sentences were selected from articles, avoiding very short or malformed sentences. One paragraph per document was selected, balanced across beginning, middle, and end. Metadata including Wikipedia URL, topic, and boolean flags for hyperlinked entities and images were extracted.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automatic checks were implemented to ensure translation quality: language identification, checking for copy of source, checking for significantly different length, checking fluency via language model, and checking for copy from public translation engines. Translations failing these checks were sent back for re-translation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Translations were performed by professional translators via Language Service Providers (LSPs). A two-step translation and quality assurance workflow was used. An initial LSP performed translation and editing. An independent LSP performed quality assurance (QA). If the QA score was below a threshold (90%), translations were sent back to the original LSP for re-translation. Evaluators assessed errors in grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition/omission, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, and register.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Translation quality was assessed using a Translation Quality Score on a 0-100 scale based on identified errors. The acceptable threshold was set at 90%. The largest error category across all languages was mistranslation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Sentence selection was performed by 10 annotators (6 male, 4 female) from various regions (East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, North America) with roles as researchers and program/project managers. Translations were performed by professional translators via LSPs.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SentencePiece BLEU (spBLEU) metric was used for evaluation. Automatic checks included language identification, length checks, fluency checks via language model, and similarity checks against commercial translation engines.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly released. The test set is available via a publicly available evaluation server to prevent overfitting. The authors hope to continue expanding the number of languages covered.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to foster progress in the machine translation community, particularly for low-resource languages. It supports the evaluation of many-to-many multilingual translation systems and helps address the lack of high-quality evaluation benchmarks for languages spoken by the majority of the world's population.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The source sentences are from English Wikipedia, which may introduce biases present in Wikipedia content. The selection process aimed for topic diversity (news, children's books, travel) to mitigate domain bias. However, the reliance on English as the source language for all translations introduces a potential bias towards English-centric perspectives.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset consists of only 3001 sentences. Source sentences are in English, meaning translations into other languages are essentially translations of translations if the target language is not English. Performance varies significantly by language resource level and family. Some low-resource languages have very few professional translators available, which can impact quality and consistency.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of many-to-many multilingual machine translation models, document-level translation, multimodal translation, sentence and document classification, language identification, and multilingual domain adaptation.
